question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(-1.55<Z<1.55).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9236\,$ | $\,0.9251\,$ | $\,0.9265\,$ |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9370\,$ | $\,0.9382\,$ | $\,0.9394\,$ |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9484\,$ | $\,0.9495\,$ | $\,0.9505\,$ |

$P(-1.55<Z<1.55)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-1.55<Z<1.55).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/45d71abed85d91a5a1b150fb741bcc8fa9967f7b2b8d77df35423a909b1e8522.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.55<Z<1.55) & =P(Z<1.55)-P(Z\le -1.55) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.55)-P(Z\le -1.55) \\  & =Φ(1.55)-Φ(-1.55)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(1.55)=0.9394,
$$

but we are not given $Φ(-1.55).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.55) & =P(Z\le -1.55) \\  & =P(Z\ge 1.55) \\  & =1-P(Z<1.55) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1.55) \\  & =1-Φ(1.55) \\  & =1-0.9394 \\  & =0.0606\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.55<Z<1.55) & =Φ(1.55)-Φ(-1.55) \\  & =0.9394-0.0606 \\  & =0.8788.\end{aligned}
$$
